reason: The cited evidence (E1) concerns a TiCoCrFeMn alloy without tungsten, showing grain stability and hardness retention after 100 h at 1000 °C, but it provides no data on tungsten addition, W-rich precipitate formation, or grain boundary pinning in any alloy. The key premises about tungsten's role are entirely unsupported by the cited passage.
premises: Tungsten addition forms stable W-rich precipitates at grain boundaries in Ti-Ni-primary HEAs
These precipitates pin grain boundaries and inhibit grain coarsening at 1000 °C
Grain boundary pinning preserves microhardness during prolonged high-temperature exposure
The cited TiCoCrFeMn alloy behavior (grain stability, hardness) is transferable to Ti-Ni-primary systems
